Facts:
- In 1619, the tune of "God Save the Queen" was sometimes attributed to John Bull.
- The author of the tune of "God Save the Queen" is unknown, and the tune may originate in plainchant.
- "God Save the Queen", or "God Save the King" when the reigning monarch is male, is the national or royal anthem in a number of Commonwealth realms, their territories, and the British Crown Dependencies.
- At that time, the Australian Government decided to scrap "God Save the Queen" as the national anthem and ran the "Australian National Anthem Quest" to find a replacement.
- "Give Me a Home Among the Gumtrees" was Johnson and Brown's response to the "Australian National Anthem Quest".
- "Give Me a Home Among the Gumtrees" did not win the "Australian National Anthem Quest".
